How to use the MGRS map tool

Mark, measure and share positions on a map of Finland, with the R and D areas, APP-6 symbols and MGRS coordinates in one place.

The screen

The map fills most of the screen. Everything else sits around its edges, and the panel on the left can be hidden.

  1. 1Panel tabs. Areas, Layers, Symbols and Settings. On a computer, the Panel button at the top right hides the panel.
  2. 2Toolbar. Choose what to do on the map. Tap a tool again to put it away.
  3. 3Drawing bar. Appears while a tool is in use. It shows what to do next, live measurements, and the buttons to finish.
  4. 4Map controls. Search, background map and areas, your location, all of Finland, area lock, full map, and zoom.
  5. 5Coordinate readout. MGRS of the mouse pointer, or of the crosshair on a phone. Tap it to copy.
  6. 6Your drawings on top of the R areas (red) and D areas (orange, dashed).

The tools

Each tool stays on until you press Done or the cross in the drawing bar, so you can add several things in a row.

PanMove the map and open things. Tap a drawing to see its details, actions and corner handles.
PointAdd plain points, for example waypoints.
SymbolPlace the APP-6 symbol chosen in the Symbols tab.
MeasureDistance and direction between two places. Save as many as you need.
VectorAn arrow from a start point, with a distance and a direction.
LineA route or a line with its length and each leg.
PolygonAn area with any number of corners, with its area and perimeter.
CircleA center and a radius, for example a safety zone.
RectangleTwo opposite corners. Its sides run north to south and east to west.

Searching

The magnifier at the top of the map controls opens one search for everything: places and addresses, coordinates, R and D areas, and the things you have drawn.

  • Places and addresses: towns, villages, streets, house numbers, and named terrain such as hills and lakes.
  • Coordinates: MGRS or any format the coordinate panel accepts.
  • R and D areas: by code or name.
  • Your drawings: by the name you gave them.

Use the arrow keys and Enter, or tap a result. A place opens with its MGRS and a Save as point button that keeps the place name.

On a computer, Ctrl + K or / opens the search.

Place search uses Photon, a free service built on OpenStreetMap data, so what you type there is sent to it. Coordinates, areas and your drawings are searched on your own device. If Photon cannot be reached, press Enter to try OpenStreetMap's own search instead.

Placing things on the map

You choose how a tap on the map is treated. This keeps accidental taps from adding things while you move the map with your finger.

Tap

A single tap adds. Fastest with a mouse. On a computer, double-click finishes a line or polygon.

Hold

Keep your finger still for half a second. A ring fills up, the phone buzzes, and the item is added. The default on phones.

Crosshair

Taps do nothing. Move the map until the crosshair is on the spot, then press Add at crosshair. The most precise way.

Switch modes with the small chip in the drawing bar (it reads Tap, Hold or Crosshair), or in Settings. On a phone, Add at crosshair is always there as well.

Points and symbols

Points are plain markers. Symbols are APP-6 map symbols: units, equipment, installations, control measures and more.

Choosing a symbol

  1. Open the Symbols tab.
  2. Pick the affiliation: friend, hostile, neutral or unknown.
  3. Search by name, in English or in Finnish for common symbols (jalkaväki, kranaatinheitin, tulenjohtopaikka). You can also browse by category.
  4. Set echelon, headquarters, task force, planned, the two modifiers, the designation and the higher formation as needed.
  5. Press Place on map, or Add by coordinates to place it at a typed grid.

The last symbols you used appear under Recently used. All 1 168 APP-6D point symbols that the symbol library can draw are in the list. If you know a symbol's 20-digit SIDC code, you can type it straight into the field under the preview.

Details and changes

Tap a symbol or point to see its MGRS, latitude and longitude, and actions. Tap the MGRS to copy it.

Edit symbol loads it into the Symbols tab with an orange Editing bar. Change what you need and press Save changes.

The name at the top of the details can be edited directly.

Measuring and vectors

A measurement gives the distance and direction from one place to another. A vector is an arrow drawn from a start point by distance and direction.

Measure

  1. Choose Measure and place the start point, then the end point.
  2. Press Save measurement to keep it in the selected layer. Place a new start point to measure again.

Vector

Choose Vector and place the start and end on the map, or press Type coordinates and enter a start grid, a distance and a direction. The drawing bar has a Direction in selector, and the vector keeps that unit in its label.

Directions and units

Directions can be shown and typed in five units. Choose the display unit in Settings. Where you type a direction, a unit selector sits next to the field.

UnitFull circleHow to type itShown as
Degrees36045 or 45°045.0°
Degrees, minutes, seconds36045 30 15 or 45°30'15"045°30′15″
NATO mils6400800 mil0800 mil
Finnish mils (piiru)60007-50, 750v or 750ᵛ7-50ᵛ
Minutes of angle21 6002700 MOA2700 MOA

A plain number uses the unit chosen next to the field. A sign you type always wins, so 800 mil is read as NATO mils even if Degrees is selected. Changing the unit selector converts what you have already typed, so the direction stays the same.

True north or grid north

True north points to the North Pole. Grid north follows the MGRS grid lines on the map. In Finland the two differ by up to a few degrees, more the further you are from the middle of a UTM zone.

If you work with a gridded map and a protractor, choose Grid north in Settings. Directions are then marked “(grid)” in the details and the drawing bar.

Lines and shapes

Lines, polygons, circles and rectangles go into the layer marked as active. The drawing bar shows the length, area or radius while you draw.

  • Line and polygon: place one point after another. Press Finish, or double-click on a computer in Tap mode. A polygon also closes when you place a point on its first corner.
  • Circle: place the center, then the edge, or type the radius in kilometres in the drawing bar.
  • Rectangle: place two opposite corners.
  • Undo point removes the last point. Discard throws the shape away.
  • Type coordinates moves the points you have placed so far into the coordinate panel, where you can correct them.

The details of a line or polygon list every leg with its distance and direction.

Adding by coordinates

Type or paste coordinates instead of tapping, or load them from a text file. You see the result on the map before you add it.

  1. Open it from the Layers tab (Add by coordinates), from the Symbols tab, or from Type coordinates in the drawing bar.
  2. Choose what to make: points, symbols, line, polygon, circle, rectangle, measurement or vector.
  3. Enter one coordinate per line. Text before or after a coordinate becomes its name, for example OP North 35VLH5900075500. In a line, polygon or measurement it names that point of the shape.
  4. Check the list under the box. It shows how each line was read, and which lines could not be read.
  5. Press Add to map, or Ctrl + Enter.
FormatExample
MGRS, any precision35V LH 59000 75500
35VLH5900075500
35VLH590755
Decimal degrees, dot or comma61.0650, 24.4400
61,0650; 24,4400
Degrees, minutes, seconds61°02'30"N 24°23'00"E
N 61° 02.5' E 24° 23.0'
Compact DMS, as in the AIP610230N 0242300E
GeoJSONPaste it or load the file. It is imported as layers.

Named points in lines and polygons

Names you give to the points of a line, polygon or measurement appear next to the points on the map, in the start and end rows and legs of the details, in copied coordinates, and in exports and share links.

Edit coordinates lists the points with their names in front. Change the text in front of a coordinate to rename that point. For a point or symbol, the name is on its coordinate line in the same way.

For a line or polygon made from points, keeping the same number of lines renames and moves the points themselves, and the shape stays linked. Adding or removing lines turns it into an ordinary shape that keeps the names.

Decimal pairs are read as latitude, longitude. If yours come as longitude, latitude (GeoJSON or KML order), tick Decimal pairs are lon, lat. In Finland the tool cannot tell the order by itself, because both numbers are below 90.

Editing and moving

Tap any drawing to open its details. From there you can rename, copy, move, reshape, change layer or delete it.

Hold, then drag

To stop things moving by accident, points, symbols and corners only move after you hold them still for about half a second. A ring fills, the phone buzzes and the item lifts with a shadow. Now drag it. A quick touch or swipe never moves anything; it just pans the map.

You can change this in Settings under Moving points and corners: hold then drag (the default), drag straight away, or off.

Moving the corners of a shape

  1. Tap the shape. White handles appear on its corners together with its details.
  2. Hold a handle, then drag it. The details close and the edit bar with Done appears. From now on the corners drag straight away, so you can move several in a row.
  3. Finish with Done, or by tapping empty map.

If the details cover a corner, close them with the ×; the handles stay until you tap the map. Small handles between corners add a corner. Double-click a corner to remove it. On a line made from points, moving a corner moves that point.

Edit shape in the details goes straight to editing, even when dragging is switched off.

Circles

Type a new radius in the circle's details, in metres, kilometres or nautical miles, and press Apply. The centre stays where it is.

In Edit shape the edit bar has the same field. Dragging the edge handle updates the number, so you can drag roughly and then type the exact value.

Other ways to move things

  • Move… moves by a distance in a direction, for example 250 m to 4800 mil. It works for a single item or a whole selection.
  • Edit coordinates opens the coordinate panel with the current grids and names, ready to correct.

Deleting and moving by distance can be undone from the message at the bottom of the screen.

Layers and selecting

Layers keep your drawings in groups, for example own forces, enemy and routes. Each has a name, a colour and a show or hide switch.

The layer list

  • The round button marks the layer new drawings go into.
  • The colour square changes the layer's colour.
  • Tap the name to open the list of items. Tap an item to zoom to it.
  • The eye shows or hides the layer.

Selecting several items

Tick items one by one, or tick the box next to a layer to select all of it. The orange bar then lets you move them to another layer, copy their coordinates, move them by a distance, share them or delete them.

Lines and polygons from points

Tick points in the order you want them joined, then press Line from points or Polygon from points. The shape is drawn dashed, and it follows the points: move a point and the shape moves with it.

To stop a shape from following its points, press Unlink in its details.

R and D areas

The Finnish restricted (R) and danger (D) areas are always available, with every corner point in MGRS.

  • Search the Areas tab by code or name (122, Lohtaja), or tap an area on the map.
  • The search box also takes a coordinate. Type an MGRS grid to get a Go to option, and save that spot as a point if you want.
  • Precision (1 m, 10 m or 100 m) and the spaced or compact format apply to the grids shown everywhere in the tool.

Keeping areas out of the way

The lock button in the map controls makes the areas ignore taps, so they no longer open when you tap near them while drawing. They stay visible.

The map menu (the stacked-layers button) hides R or D areas, or all of them at once, and switches the background between OpenStreetMap, a topographic map and aerial imagery.

The area data is unofficial and not for navigation. Always check the current AIP, NOTAMs and Traficom publications.

Sharing and files

Share a layer, a selection or everything as a link. The items travel inside the link itself, so nothing is uploaded anywhere.

SharePress Share in the Layers tab, in a layer's actions or in the selection bar.
SendCopy the link, send it with the phone's share menu, send it as a GeoJSON file, or let the other phone scan the QR code.
ImportThe receiver opens the link and presses Import. The items arrive as new layers. Nothing they already have changes.

Anyone who sees the link can read what is in it, and messaging apps keep a copy. Do not share sensitive or operational information this way.

Files

  • Export GeoJSON keeps everything, including symbols, circles, measurements and vectors, and can be imported back.
  • Export KML is for Google Earth and other map programs.
  • Import GeoJSON adds layers from a file.

Using a phone

On a phone the panel becomes a sheet at the bottom. Tap a tab to open it and tap it again to close it, or swipe the bar up and down.

  • The full map button (four corners, bottom of the map controls) hides the sheet and shrinks the toolbar to the current tool. Press it again to bring the menus back. On Android it also switches to fullscreen.
  • Tap the tool name in the drawing bar to fold the bar to a single line.
  • On an iPhone, Share › Add to Home Screen opens the tool without the browser bar.
  • The crosshair in the middle of the map is where the readout and Add at crosshair point.
  • To move a point or a corner, hold it until it lifts, then drag. A quick swipe over it just pans the map.

Settings

  • Coordinates: precision and format of every MGRS shown.
  • Directions: display unit, and true or grid north.
  • Placing things on the map: tap, hold or crosshair.
  • Moving points and corners: hold then drag, drag straight away, or off.
  • Map: names of your drawings on the map, and the area lock.
  • User guide: the link at the top opens this page.

Keyboard shortcuts

EscDiscard the shape you are drawing, then leave the tool, then close the details EnterFinish a line or polygon BackspaceUndo the last point Ctrl + EnterAdd from the coordinate panel Ctrl + K or /Open the search

Good to know

  • Your drawings are saved in this browser only. Another browser or phone does not see them. Share or export to keep a copy or move them.
  • Distances and areas are great-circle values on a sphere, accurate to about 0.5 %.
  • MGRS values are truncated, not rounded, as the MGRS standard requires.
  • The R and D area corners come from sources given to the nearest second (about 30 m). Digits beyond 100 m precision only reflect that rounding.
  • The background maps and place search need an internet connection. The tool itself, the areas and your drawings keep working without one once the page has loaded.
